name: Reclaim
shape: Under last week's low, then back above it by the close.
description: Every other screen here watches a stock come up to a ceiling. This one watches a floor break and not stay broken. Last week's low is a price anyone can see, so it is where the stops are; a stock that trades through it and closes back above has taken them out and found nobody willing to sell lower. Only stocks that were in good order the session before are listed: above their 50-day line, the 50 above the 200, within 15% of their high, and rated 80 or better for relative strength. The level shown is the low that was broken, and the first bucket holds the names still under it with a session left to come back. A reclaim is listed for twenty sessions, and a close back under the level ends it. Before this screen was published it was run over two years of real prices: 12,947 reclaims in 2,547 stocks, with no relative-strength test. Twenty sessions on, the median one was down 0.3%, where the median session of a stock in the same good order was up 0.6%, and a little over half had closed back under the level inside five sessions. No setting of any dial changed that. So read this as a list of leaders that were just shaken and held, which is a fact about the chart, and not as a reason to expect anything. What becomes of each one is counted from the first night on the follow-through page.

concepts.title: The level
concepts.text: The lowest price of the calendar week before.

concepts.title: The undercut
concepts.text: A session that trades beneath it.

concepts.title: The reclaim
concepts.text: A close back above it, that session or the next, in the upper half of its range.

funnel.title: The liquid US universe
funnel.text: US common stocks over $5, market cap over $300M, and at least $5M traded a day over the last 20 sessions.

funnel.title: Leadership
funnel.text: Relative strength rating of 80 or better.

funnel.title: In good order the session before
funnel.text: It closed above its 50-day average the session before it broke last week's low.

funnel.title: An uptrend, not a bounce
funnel.text: Its 50-day average was above its 200-day average that session.

funnel.title: Near its highs
funnel.text: That session it closed within 15% of its 52-week high.

funnel.title: A dip under it, not a break
funnel.text: Its low was no more than 4% beneath last week's low.

funnel.title: Back above it quickly
funnel.text: It closed back above the level on the session it broke it, or within 1 more.

funnel.title: And closed well
funnel.text: The session that took it back closed in the upper part of its own range: at least 50% of the way from its low to its high.

funnel_preface: Every number below is a dial you can move in Filters.

params.label: Lowest RS rating we'll accept
params.funnel_text: Relative strength rating of {value} or better.
params.help: Ten points stricter than the base screens. Every stock in an uptrend dips under last week's low a few times a year, so the level itself narrows nothing; relative strength is the filter with published support behind it, and here it does the narrowing.

params.label: Above its 50-day line going in
params.funnel_title: In good order the session before
params.funnel_text: It closed above its 50-day average the session before it broke last week's low.
params.help: Judged the session before the undercut, not on the day. On the day the stock is under a level, which says nothing about the trend it came from.

params.label: 50-day above the 200-day going in
params.funnel_text: Its 50-day average was above its 200-day average that session.
params.help: A stock under a falling 200-day line breaks last week's low most weeks. A stock with under 200 sessions of history is not judged on this.

params.label: Furthest below its 52-week high going in
params.funnel_text: That session it closed within {value}% of its 52-week high.
params.help: A pullback in a stock near its highs. Further down than this and last week's low is one of several floors already given up.

params.label: Furthest it may go under the level
params.funnel_title: A dip under it, not a break
params.funnel_text: Its low was no more than {value}% beneath last week's low.
params.help: Past this it is a breakdown that happened to bounce, not stops being taken at a level.

params.label: Sessions it has to close back above
params.funnel_text: It closed back above the level on the session it broke it, or within {value} more.
params.help: Zero is the strict form: under it and back above it in one session. The longer it stays under, the less it is a sweep and the more it is simply a lower price.

params.label: Where in its range the reclaim closed
params.funnel_text: The session that took it back closed in the upper part of its own range: at least {value}% of the way from its low to its high.
params.help: A close back above the level that is also near the session's low was sold into. Zero turns this off.

params.label: How long a reclaim stays listed
params.help: Twenty sessions is the middle distance its record is measured over. After that it is a stock in a trend, which the other screens cover.

params.label: How recent counts as fresh
params.help: A breakout stays in the fresh bucket for this many sessions before it moves to climbing.

trade_steps.title: Buy the breakout
trade_steps.text: As it pushes through the pivot.

trade_steps.title: Set a safety net
trade_steps.text: An automatic exit if it drops about 8% from where you got in.

trade_steps.title: Lock in "no loss"
trade_steps.text: Once it is up enough, move that net to where you started.

trade_steps.title: Ride the trend
trade_steps.text: Raise the net as it climbs.

trade_steps_preface: Risk is decided before entry — about 1.5% of capital on any one trade.
